Orientation of buildings and dwelling units in impacted noise areas is another technique that will be used to minimize the problem. The first row of housing adjacent to the expressway in Area One will be designed to provide adequate shielding so that only a single row of housing will need special treatment. As much parking as possible will be located along Grayland Avenue, backed up with continuous rows of housing, only interrupted by the north-south streets. Special acoustical treatment, as outlined above, will then be necessary on sides of the buildings facing the expressway and the north-south streets. Wherever possible bedroom areas within individual dwelling units will be located away from expressway frontage.
(6) The Proposed Remedial Measures: The noise impact of the Expressway on the project area will be effectively attenuated by a combination of the various measures described previously. Construction methods, building orientation, and noise barriers will be used separately or in tandem to reduce the noise levels to HUD acceptable levels. Exhibit No. 8 outlines in graphic form the proposed remedial measures that will be incorporated into the Randolph Project Plans: 
(a) West of Meadow Street: The area from Meadow Street to the western project boundary contains residential structures on both sides of the Expressway. In addition, the West End Elementary School, a church, and two other nonresidential structures occupy the area between Meadow Street and Shields Avenue. The residences are in the Rehabilitation Area. Changes accomplished during rehabilitation will provide acoustical shielding for any residential building not protected by a landscaped 15-foot earth berm. The nonresidential uses, as mentioned previously, will not receive acoustical shielding. However, the West End School, although not a residential structure will probably be treated with some type of acoustic shielding. The proper type of noise reduction methods will be determined after specific study on specific nonresidential uses has been made.
